title: Looking beyond the baseline: how scenario synthesis helps assess risks
gist: ECB staff explain 'scenario synthesis', which weights baseline and alternative scenarios to match reference risk measures (market-implied, SPF, QRA). Applied to Middle East conflict scenarios in 2026, markets put more weight on adverse/severe inflation outcomes than forecasters, with relevance shifting around the US–Iran memorandum and renewed July tensions.

themes.theme: Why the ECB needs scenarios beyond the baseline

insights.claim: The ECB Governing Council does not focus solely on the most likely forecast for inflation and growth; it also assesses risks and uncertainty around the outlook using statistical risk measures, the staff quantitative risk assessment (QRA), and sensitivity and scenario analysis.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: ECB policy decisions weigh the risk distribution, not just the point forecast, so risk-assessment shifts can move policy even with an unchanged baseline.
insights.quote: When the ECB’s Governing Council makes monetary policy decisions, it does not focus solely on the most likely forecast for inflation and growth.

insights.claim: According to the ECB, no single approach captures every aspect of uncertainty; each risk tool offers a different perspective on the risks facing the economy.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Expect the ECB to triangulate across multiple risk tools rather than anchor on one model.
insights.quote: No single approach captures every aspect of uncertainty – each offers a different perspective on the risks facing the economy.
insights.locator: To do so, the ECB uses

insights.claim: Scenario analysis complements statistical risk measures by providing narratives: it explores specific risk events such as an energy shock, geopolitical escalation, trade disruption or tighter financial conditions and illustrates the channels through which they affect inflation and growth.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: The ECB's scenario set signals which specific shocks (energy, geopolitics, trade, financial conditions) it considers policy-relevant.
insights.quote: Scenarios explore specific risk events such as an energy shock, a geopolitical escalation, a trade disruption or tighter financial conditions
insights.locator: Scenario analysis complements the statistical risk

insights.claim: During structural change or heightened geopolitical stress, risk measures based mainly on past events and data may understate the risks and the range of possible outcomes, which scenarios help address.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: In regime shifts, historically calibrated risk bands are likely too narrow; scenario tails deserve more weight.
insights.quote: risk measures based mainly on past events and data may understate the risks involved and the range of possible outcomes

insights.claim: In March 2022 ECB staff projections, the statistical risk band around the baseline 2022 HICP inflation forecast of 5.1% year-on-year, built on historical model residuals, did not capture the actual outcome of 8.4%.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Residual-based uncertainty bands materially underestimated the post-invasion inflation surge; treat such bands skeptically in shock periods.
insights.quote: did not capture the actual inflation outcome of 8.4% year-on-year

insights.claim: The adverse and severe scenarios in March 2022, centred around 5.9% and 7.1% HICP inflation respectively, highlighted risks that historical residuals alone missed and brought the risk assessment closer to what ultimately occurred.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Scenario tails proved a better guide than statistical bands during the energy crisis, supporting their growing role in ECB policy.
insights.quote: the adverse and severe scenarios, respectively concentrated around 5.9% and 7.1%, highlighted risks that historical residuals alone would have missed

insights.claim: Reference risk measures such as the Eurosystem QRA, options-implied distributions from financial markets, or professional forecasters' probability assessments show the balance of risks but lack an underlying narrative and do not explain why risk perceptions shift.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Market-implied inflation distributions alone don't explain drivers; pairing them with scenarios gives a narrative for repricing.
insights.quote: However, they do not come with an underlying narrative; nor do they explain the relative importance of individual risk events or why risk perceptions are shifting.
insights.locator: Scenario synthesis: linking narratives and risk measures

insights.claim: Scenario synthesis combines the baseline outlook with alternative scenarios by assigning each a weight so that the resulting synthetic distribution best matches an overall reference risk measure.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Gives a quantitative way to map market or survey risk pricing onto named ECB scenarios.
insights.quote: It combines the baseline outlook with a set of alternative scenarios in a way that best matches one of these overall reference risk measures.
insights.locator: Scenario synthesis provides that missing link.

insights.claim: Scenario synthesis weights should not be read as probabilities that scenarios will materialise; they indicate how relevant each scenario is for representing the risks in the reference measure, given the other scenarios included.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Avoid misreading ECB scenario weights as event probabilities in market commentary.
insights.quote: Importantly, these weights should not be interpreted as probabilities that the scenarios will materialise.
insights.locator: Scenario synthesis provides that missing link.

insights.claim: The ECB uses scenario synthesis in three ways: assessing scenario relevance against different risk measures, tracking how relevance evolves over time with frequently updated market measures, and checking whether the scenario set covers a broad enough range of risks.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Signals the ECB will increasingly reference market-implied risk shifts when communicating scenario relevance.

themes.theme: Middle East conflict: markets vs forecasters

insights.claim: For euro area HICP inflation in Q1 2027, the market-based risk measure in June 2026 was more dispersed than baseline uncertainty, with substantially more probability mass at higher inflation rates.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Markets were pricing materially more upside inflation risk than ECB baseline uncertainty implied.
insights.quote: The market-based measure is more dispersed, with substantially more probability mass at higher inflation rates.

insights.claim: The Survey of Professional Forecasters' Q2 2026 risk measure was close to the ECB baseline, somewhat narrower and peaking at a slightly lower inflation rate than baseline.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: A gap between SPF and market inflation risk pricing indicates potential mispricing or a risk premium to monitor.
insights.quote: By contrast, the SPF’s measure is close to the baseline, although somewhat narrower and with its peak at a slightly lower inflation rate.

insights.claim: Scenario synthesis weights show professional forecasters closest to the baseline, while financial markets placed more weight on the adverse and severe Middle East conflict scenarios from the June 2026 Eurosystem staff projections.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Market inflation pricing was skewed toward adverse geopolitical outcomes relative to forecasters.
insights.quote: professional forecasters remain closest to the baseline. Meanwhile, financial markets place more weight on the adverse and severe scenarios.

themes.theme: Shifting market risk perceptions and scenario coverage

insights.claim: By 30 June 2026, around the ceasefire and the Memorandum of Understanding agreed between the United States and Iran on 26 June, markets saw lower euro area inflation risks than on 11 June, with the milder scenario becoming more relevant.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Geopolitical de-escalation quickly compressed market-implied euro area inflation risk.
insights.quote: by 30 June, around the announcement of a ceasefire in the Middle East, markets saw lower inflation risks than on 11 June, although uncertainty remained

insights.claim: By 23 July 2026, renewed regional tensions heightened energy supply concerns, market-based inflation risks rose again, and the adverse scenario was seen by markets as most relevant.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Energy-supply fears remain the key transmission channel from Middle East tensions to euro area inflation risk pricing.
insights.quote: By 23 July, the geopolitical conflict had intensified further such that the adverse scenario was seen by the markets as most relevant.
insights.locator: Panel b shows how the scenarios’ relative relevance

insights.claim: Synthetic distributions captured market-implied inflation risks reasonably well on both 11 June and 30 June 2026 despite the shift in perceptions, suggesting the ECB scenario set spans the relevant range of risks.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: ECB scenarios appear to bracket market risk pricing, implying limited unmodelled tail risk as of mid-2026.
insights.quote: Despite this shift, the synthetic distributions capture the market-implied risks reasonably well at both dates.
insights.locator: Assessing scenario set coverage of market-based risks

insights.claim: Scenario synthesis does not replace expert judgement, which remains essential for selecting scenarios, building their distributions and choosing the reference risk measure; it provides a transparent framework to monitor risk shifts, assess coverage and communicate uncertainty.
insights.speaker: European Central Bank
insights.so_what: Expect ECB communication on uncertainty to lean more on scenario-based framing tied to market and survey measures.
insights.quote: Scenario synthesis does not replace expert judgement.
